notes.definition: Unreactive metals such as gold are found in the Earth as the metal itself, but most metals are found as compounds and must be extracted by chemical reactions. Metals less reactive than carbon can be extracted from their oxides by reduction with carbon, where reduction is the loss of oxygen.
explanation: A few very unreactive metals, such as gold, are found in the Earth's crust as the uncombined metal. They have not reacted with oxygen, water or other substances over millions of years, so they can simply be dug up and separated from the rock. Most metals, however, are more reactive and are found combined with other elements as compounds, often as metal oxides. A rock that contains enough of a metal compound to be worth extracting is called an ore. To get the metal out, a chemical reaction is needed.

Many metals are found as oxides, so extracting them means removing the oxygen. The loss of oxygen is reduction. Carbon is a cheap and useful reducing substance: when a metal oxide that is less reactive than carbon is heated with carbon, the carbon takes the oxygen away from the metal. For example, 2CuO(s) + C(s) → 2Cu(s) + CO₂(g). The copper oxide is reduced to copper, and the carbon is oxidised to carbon dioxide. Zinc, iron, tin, lead and copper can all be extracted this way.

The position of the metal in the reactivity series decides the method. Carbon sits between magnesium (and aluminium) and zinc. A metal below carbon is less reactive than carbon, so carbon can remove oxygen from its oxide. A metal above carbon, such as aluminium, magnesium or sodium, is more reactive than carbon, so heating its oxide with carbon has no effect. These reactive metals are extracted using electrolysis, which is more expensive because it needs large amounts of electricity.

Reduction with carbon is also a redox reaction: one substance is reduced and another is oxidised at the same time. Iron is extracted from iron oxide (Fe₂O₃) in industry. The main reaction can be written with carbon, 2Fe₂O₃(s) + 3C(s) → 4Fe(l) + 3CO₂(g), or with carbon monoxide made from the carbon, Fe₂O₃(s) + 3CO(g) → 2Fe(l) + 3CO₂(g). In both, iron oxide loses oxygen and is reduced, while carbon or carbon monoxide gains oxygen and is oxidised. You do not need to learn the details of industrial processes, but you should be able to interpret information about one if given it.

In the exam you may be given information about an unfamiliar extraction process, such as data about energy use, costs or the reactivity of the metals involved. Use the reactivity series to explain why a method works: a more reactive element can remove oxygen (or another non-metal) from a less reactive metal. For example, titanium is extracted from titanium chloride using sodium or magnesium, which are more reactive than titanium. When evaluating, compare factors such as the energy needed, the cost of raw materials, the amount of waste and the carbon dioxide released.
keyFacts: Unreactive metals such as gold are found in the Earth as the metal itself.
Most metals are found as compounds and need chemical reactions to extract the metal.
Reduction is the loss of oxygen.
Metals less reactive than carbon can be extracted from their oxides by reduction with carbon.
Example: 2CuO(s) + C(s) → 2Cu(s) + CO₂(g): copper oxide is reduced, carbon is oxidised.
Zinc, iron and copper can be extracted using carbon.
Metals more reactive than carbon (such as aluminium) cannot be extracted using carbon; electrolysis is used instead.
Electrolysis is more expensive than reduction with carbon because it uses large amounts of electricity.
An ore is a rock containing enough of a metal compound to make extraction worthwhile.

keyTerms.definition: The process of obtaining a metal from its compound, usually from an ore.
A rock that contains enough of a metal or metal compound to make extracting the metal worthwhile.
The loss of oxygen from a substance.
The gain of oxygen by a substance.
A metal found in the Earth as the uncombined element, such as gold.
Using electricity to break down an ionic compound; used to extract metals more reactive than carbon.

workedExamples.title: Choosing an extraction method
workedExamples.question: Explain whether each metal can be extracted by heating its oxide with carbon: (a) zinc, (b) aluminium.
steps: Find each metal in the reactivity series and compare it with carbon.
(a) Zinc is below carbon, so carbon is more reactive and can remove oxygen from zinc oxide: 2ZnO + C → 2Zn + CO₂.
(b) Aluminium is above carbon, so carbon is less reactive and cannot remove the oxygen. Aluminium must be extracted by electrolysis.
workedExamples.answer: (a) Yes, zinc is less reactive than carbon. (b) No, aluminium is more reactive than carbon, so electrolysis is used.

workedExamples.title: Mass of metal from an oxide
workedExamples.question: Calculate the maximum mass of iron that can be extracted from 320 tonnes of iron oxide, Fe₂O₃. (Ar: Fe = 56, O = 16)
steps: Fraction of the mass that is iron = 112 ÷ 160 = 0.70 (70%).

workedExamples.title: Mass of metal in an ore
workedExamples.question: A copper ore contains 2.5% copper by mass. Calculate the mass of copper in 400 tonnes of ore.
steps: Convert the percentage to a decimal: 2.5% = 0.025.
This shows why huge amounts of rock must be mined and why waste rock is a problem.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think all metals are found in the ground as pure metal.
misconceptions.right: Only very unreactive metals such as gold are found as the metal itself. Most metals are found as compounds, such as oxides, and must be extracted chemically.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think carbon can extract any metal from its oxide if the temperature is high enough.
misconceptions.right: Carbon can only reduce oxides of metals that are less reactive than carbon. Aluminium and magnesium oxides cannot be reduced by carbon, so electrolysis is used.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the metal is oxidised during extraction because oxygen is involved.
misconceptions.right: The metal oxide loses oxygen, so it is reduced. It is the carbon that gains oxygen and is oxidised.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think electrolysis is used for every metal because it is the most modern method.
misconceptions.right: Electrolysis is expensive because it uses a lot of electricity, so it is only used when carbon reduction is not possible.

realWorld: Iron is extracted in a blast furnace by reducing iron oxide with carbon (as carbon monoxide); it is then made into steel for buildings, cars and bridges.
Aluminium is extracted by electrolysis, so aluminium smelters are often built near cheap sources of electricity such as hydroelectric power stations.
Gold has been found as nuggets and flakes in rivers and rocks for thousands of years because it is so unreactive.
Steel makers are testing hydrogen instead of carbon to reduce iron oxide, which produces water instead of carbon dioxide.
examTips: Always compare the metal with carbon: 'iron is less reactive than carbon, so carbon can remove the oxygen from iron oxide'.
Use the words reduced and oxidised precisely and name the full substance: 'iron oxide is reduced; carbon is oxidised'.
You will not be asked to recall the details of industrial processes, but you may need to interpret information about one. Read the data carefully and use it in your answer.
In percentage calculations, remember to multiply the Ar by the number of atoms of the metal in the formula (two Fe atoms in Fe₂O₃).
In evaluation questions, give both advantages and disadvantages and finish with a justified conclusion.
summary: Gold and other very unreactive metals are found as the metal itself.
Most metals are found as compounds and need chemical reactions to extract them.
Reduction is the loss of oxygen.
Metals less reactive than carbon are extracted by heating their oxides with carbon.
In carbon reduction, the metal oxide is reduced and the carbon is oxidised.
Metals more reactive than carbon are extracted by electrolysis, which is more expensive.

questions.question: Which metal is found in the Earth as the metal itself?
markScheme: 1 mark: gold
questions.explanation: Gold is very unreactive, so it does not form compounds easily and is found as the uncombined metal. Iron, aluminium and sodium are found as compounds.

questions.question: Which metal can be extracted by heating its oxide with carbon?
markScheme: 1 mark: iron
questions.explanation: Iron is less reactive than carbon, so carbon can remove the oxygen from iron oxide. Potassium, magnesium and aluminium are all more reactive than carbon.

questions.question: During the extraction of a metal from its oxide, the metal oxide is reduced. What does reduced mean here?
markScheme: 1 mark: it loses oxygen
questions.explanation: Reduction is the loss of oxygen. Heating may be needed to make the reaction happen, but it is not what 'reduced' means.

questions.question:
Zinc oxide is heated with carbon:
2ZnO(s) + C(s) → 2Zn(s) + CO₂(g)
Which substance is oxidised?
markScheme: 1 mark: carbon
questions.explanation: Carbon gains oxygen to become carbon dioxide, so carbon is oxidised. Zinc oxide loses oxygen and is reduced.

questions.question: Why is aluminium not extracted by heating aluminium oxide with carbon?
options: Aluminium oxide does not contain oxygen
Aluminium is less reactive than carbon
Aluminium is more reactive than carbon
markScheme: 1 mark: aluminium is more reactive than carbon
questions.explanation: Carbon can only remove oxygen from metals less reactive than itself. Aluminium is above carbon in the reactivity series, so electrolysis is used. Carbon is actually cheap.

questions.question: Which equation for the reduction of iron oxide by carbon is correctly balanced?
markScheme: 1 mark: 2Fe₂O₃ + 3C → 4Fe + 3CO₂
questions.explanation: Left: 4 Fe, 6 O, 3 C. Right: 4 Fe, 3 C, 6 O. The other equations do not have equal numbers of each atom on both sides.

questions.question: How are most metals found in the Earth's crust?
options: As compounds that must be reacted to get the metal
markScheme: 1 mark: as compounds that need chemical reactions to extract the metal
questions.explanation: Most metals are reactive enough to have formed compounds such as oxides. Only unreactive metals like gold are found uncombined. Alloys are made by people.

questions.question:
Titanium is extracted from titanium chloride by heating it with sodium:
TiCl₄ + 4Na → Ti + 4NaCl
What does this reaction show?
options: Sodium is more reactive than titanium
Titanium is more reactive than sodium
markScheme: 1 mark: sodium is more reactive than titanium
questions.explanation: Sodium displaces titanium from its compound, which is only possible if sodium is more reactive. This shows how unfamiliar extraction processes can be explained using the reactivity series.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows part of the reactivity series.
Metal Q is between magnesium and aluminium in the reactivity series.
Which method should be used to extract Q from its oxide?
options: Heat the oxide on its own
Dig it up as the metal
markScheme: 1 mark: electrolysis
questions.explanation: Q is above carbon, so carbon cannot reduce its oxide. Metals more reactive than carbon are extracted by electrolysis.

questions.question:
Iron oxide reacts with carbon monoxide:
Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂
Which substance gains oxygen?
markScheme: 1 mark: carbon monoxide
questions.explanation: CO becomes CO₂, gaining an oxygen atom, so carbon monoxide is oxidised. Iron oxide loses oxygen and is reduced.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows information about a copper ore.
Calculate the mass of copper in the ore.
questions.explanation: 2.5% of 400 = 0.025 × 400 = 10 tonnes. The other 390 tonnes is waste rock.

questions.question:
Calculate the percentage by mass of copper in copper oxide, CuO.
Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
Relative atomic masses (Ar): Cu = 63.5; O = 16
markScheme: 1 mark: Mr of CuO = 63.5 + 16 = 79.5
questions.explanation: 63.5 ÷ 79.5 = 0.7987..., × 100 = 79.87%, which is 79.9% to 3 significant figures.

questions.question:
Calculate the mass of zinc in 162 g of zinc oxide, ZnO.
Relative atomic masses (Ar): Zn = 65; O = 16
markScheme: 1 mark: Mr of ZnO = 65 + 16 = 81
questions.explanation: In every 81 g of zinc oxide there are 65 g of zinc. 162 g is twice 81 g, so it contains 2 × 65 = 130 g of zinc.

questions.question:
Iron is extracted from iron oxide, Fe₂O₃.
Calculate the maximum mass of iron that can be extracted from 320 tonnes of iron oxide.
Relative atomic masses (Ar): Fe = 56; O = 16
markScheme: 1 mark: Mr of Fe₂O₃ = 160
1 mark: mass of iron in formula = 2 × 56 = 112 (fraction 112 ÷ 160 = 0.7)
1 mark: 0.7 × 320 = 224 tonnes
questions.explanation: Iron makes up 112 ÷ 160 = 70% of the mass of Fe₂O₃. 70% of 320 tonnes = 224 tonnes. Using only one Fe atom (56) would give the wrong answer of 112 tonnes.

questions.question:
A low-grade ore contains 4.0% of a metal by mass.
Calculate the mass of ore that must be processed to obtain 1.0 tonne of the metal.
Assume that all of the metal is extracted.
markScheme: 1 mark: = 25 tonnes
questions.explanation: If 4.0% of the ore is metal, then mass of ore × 0.040 = 1.0 tonne, so mass of ore = 1.0 ÷ 0.040 = 25 tonnes.

questions.question: Explain why gold is found in the Earth as the metal itself.
markScheme: 1 mark: gold is very unreactive (so it has not formed compounds)
questions.explanation: Gold is at the bottom of the reactivity series, so it does not react with oxygen, water or other substances in the ground.

questions.question: Name the element that is heated with metal oxides to extract metals that are less reactive than it.
markScheme: 1 mark: carbon
questions.explanation: Carbon is cheap and is more reactive than metals such as zinc, iron and copper, so it can remove the oxygen from their oxides.

questions.question:
Copper oxide is heated with carbon.
2CuO(s) + C(s) → 2Cu(s) + CO₂(g)
Identify the substance that is reduced and the substance that is oxidised.
Give a reason for each answer.
markScheme: 1 mark: copper oxide is reduced because it loses oxygen
1 mark: carbon is oxidised because it gains oxygen
questions.explanation: The oxygen moves from the copper oxide to the carbon. Losing oxygen is reduction; gaining oxygen is oxidation.

questions.question:
Zinc oxide, ZnO, is heated with carbon to produce zinc and carbon dioxide.
Write a balanced symbol equation for this reaction.
Include state symbols.
markScheme: 1 mark: correct formulae and balancing: 2ZnO + C → 2Zn + CO₂
1 mark: state symbols (s), (s), (s), (g)
questions.explanation: CO₂ contains two oxygen atoms, which come from two ZnO, so 2ZnO and 2Zn are needed. Zinc oxide, carbon and zinc are solids; carbon dioxide is a gas.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows part of the reactivity series.
Explain why iron can be extracted from iron oxide using carbon, but magnesium cannot be extracted from magnesium oxide using carbon.
markScheme: 1 mark: iron is less reactive than carbon, so carbon can remove oxygen from iron oxide
1 mark: magnesium is more reactive than carbon, so carbon cannot remove oxygen from magnesium oxide
questions.explanation: Carbon sits between magnesium and zinc in the reactivity series. It can only reduce oxides of metals below it.

questions.question:

The gas given off turns the limewater milky.
Name the gas.

1 mark: the carbon has gained oxygen / been oxidised (by taking oxygen from the copper oxide)
questions.explanation: Limewater turns milky with carbon dioxide. The oxygen in the CO₂ came from copper oxide, so the carbon has been oxidised while the copper oxide was reduced.

questions.question: Suggest why metals are extracted by reduction with carbon whenever possible, rather than by electrolysis.
markScheme: 1 mark: electrolysis is more expensive because it uses large amounts of electricity / energy (carbon is cheap)
questions.explanation: Electrolysis needs a lot of electrical energy, often including energy to melt the ore. Carbon (as coke) is cheap and plentiful.

questions.question:
Lead is extracted from lead sulfide in two stages.
Stage 1: 2PbS + 3O₂ → 2PbO + 2SO₂
Stage 2: PbO + C → Pb + CO
Identify the stage in which a lead compound is reduced and the stage in which a lead compound is oxidised.
Explain your answer.
markScheme: 1 mark: stage 1: lead sulfide gains oxygen so it is oxidised
1 mark: stage 2: lead oxide loses oxygen so it is reduced
questions.explanation: In stage 1 the sulfide is converted into an oxide, gaining oxygen. In stage 2 carbon removes the oxygen, so lead oxide is reduced to lead.

questions.question:
Explain how the position of a metal in the reactivity series determines how the metal is obtained from the Earth.
Use examples and at least one equation in your answer.
markScheme: Indicative content: very unreactive metals such as gold are found as the metal itself and only need to be separated from rock; most metals are found as compounds, often oxides, in ores; carbon is placed in the reactivity series between aluminium/magnesium and zinc; metals less reactive than carbon (zinc, iron, lead, copper) can be extracted by heating the oxide with carbon; carbon removes the oxygen: reduction is loss of oxygen; e.g. 2CuO + C → 2Cu + CO₂ or 2ZnO + C → 2Zn + CO₂; the metal oxide is reduced and the carbon is oxidised; metals more reactive than carbon (sodium, magnesium, aluminium) cannot be reduced by carbon so are extracted by electrolysis; electrolysis is more expensive because it uses a lot of electricity.

Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): all three cases (native, carbon reduction, electrolysis) explained by comparing reactivity with carbon, with correct examples and a correct equation; reduction explained as loss of oxygen.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): at least two cases described with some explanation linked to reactivity, examples or an equation.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements, for example gold is found as a metal or iron is extracted with carbon, with little explanation.
questions.explanation: The key comparison is with carbon. The less reactive the metal, the easier it is to extract; the most unreactive metals need no chemical extraction at all.

questions.question:
Iron oxide can be reduced using carbon or using hydrogen gas made with renewable electricity.
Method A: 2Fe₂O₃ + 3C → 4Fe + 3CO₂
Method B: Fe₂O₃ + 3H₂ → 2Fe + 3H₂O
Table 1 shows information about the two methods.
Evaluate the two methods.

headers: Cost of reducing agent per tonne of iron in £
Mass of carbon dioxide released per tonne of iron in tonnes

markScheme: Indicative content: in both methods iron oxide loses oxygen and is reduced; in A carbon is oxidised to carbon dioxide, in B hydrogen is oxidised to water; method A is cheaper (£60 vs £190, about three times cheaper); method A releases far more carbon dioxide (1.8 t vs 0.1 t, 18 times as much), a greenhouse gas linked to climate change; method B's product is water, which is harmless; method B relies on a supply of renewable electricity and hydrogen, which is more expensive; conclusion: B is better for the environment, A is cheaper; a justified judgement.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): compares both methods using the data for cost and carbon dioxide, links to reduction, and reaches a justified conclusion.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple statements of an advantage or disadvantage of one or both methods, with little use of data.
questions.explanation: An evaluation needs points on both sides, use of the numbers given, and a conclusion. Both are reduction by removal of oxygen; they differ in cost and in the waste product.

markScheme: Indicative content: mix black copper oxide powder with carbon (charcoal) powder; place in a hard-glass test tube; heat strongly with a Bunsen burner; connect a delivery tube from the tube into limewater; limewater turns milky, showing carbon dioxide is made; the black mixture turns pink-brown as copper forms; remove the delivery tube from the limewater before stopping heating to prevent suck-back; allow to cool and tip out the product.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): clear method with mixing, strong heating, collecting gas through limewater, and an expected observation.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): basic idea of heating copper oxide with carbon, with little detail of the test for carbon dioxide.
questions.explanation: Carbon reduces copper oxide to copper; the carbon becomes carbon dioxide, which turns limewater milky.

questions.question: Zinc is extracted by heating zinc oxide with which element?
markScheme: 1 mark: carbon
questions.explanation: Carbon removes the oxygen from zinc oxide (reduction). Adding oxygen would oxidise, not reduce.
